D.treatment: Y2 narrowed digging task with targeted biology and disciplinary supports
D.comparison: Y1 broad search-and-rescue task with less targeted supports

O.outcome_detail: integrated design process driven by disciplinary understanding

cells.quote: Data from three focal groups (one from each year of the project) suggest that a focused design task, supported by explicit and targeted supports for science, CT, and engineering practices, led to a student technology design process that was driven by disciplinary understanding.
cells.note: The study used iterative design-based research rather than a randomized comparison; the contrast reflects curriculum iterations across years. The Y2 focal-group finding reported in the wiki entry states that all focal groups completed animal structure–function analyses, but the full text excerpt does not report a quantitative effect.

D.treatment: Y2 targeted supports for CT and disciplinary connections
D.comparison: Y1 curriculum stated CT goals but did not explicitly support them

O.outcome_detail: Participation in CT practices during the integrated robot-design process

cells.quote: Although CT goals were intended and stated in the curriculum front matter they were not explicitly supported in the student and teacher materials. We also further emphasized students’ CT practices during all activities (not just programming). Specifically, students were asked to complete a storyboard of 3 labelled sketches (abstraction) to show digging at several points of time, and also to explicitly compare and contrast animal and robot structure–function.
cells.note: The comparison is between successive design iterations in a design-based research study, not randomized conditions.

D.treatment: Y2 focused digging-robot task with targeted disciplinary resources and supports
D.comparison: Y1 broad search-and-rescue task with many possible functions and less targeted integration

O.outcome_detail: Technology design process driven by biology, engineering, and CT understanding

cells.quote: Data from three focal groups (one from each year of the project) suggest that a focused design task, supported by explicit and targeted supports for science, CT, and engineering practices, led to a student technology design process that was driven by disciplinary understanding.
cells.note: The study reports an iterative qualitative comparison across curriculum versions rather than a controlled experiment.

D.comparison: Year 3 curriculum with additional internal-anatomy supports

O.outcome_detail: Applying animal structure-function understanding to robot material choices

cells.quote: "However, we noticed that students in Year 2 were not always extending their animal structure–function understanding to the choice or use of building materials. Students were relying on pliable materials (e.g., cardboard used only in flat pieces) instead of recognizing that digging structures needed to be stronger."
cells.note: The study text supplied above does not include this finding or a direct Year 2–Year 3 outcome comparison; the quote is therefore taken from the wiki entry as permitted.
